title: Hosts
description: Machines enrolled to run your sandboxes.

empty.title: No hosts yet
empty.description: Enroll a machine below. It appears here once enrolled, and is ready when its daemon is connected.

enroll.title: Enroll a machine
enroll.description: Run these on the Linux machine that will host sandboxes, in this order.
enroll.tokenAlternative: Prefer a long-lived token? Mint one on the Host credentials page.

steps.install: On a Linux machine with KVM, Incus 6.14 or newer and the br_netfilter module, install wssp from this server as the user that will run the daemon (not root). The installer checks the download's checksum and prints the next steps.
steps.enroll: Enroll it (replace my-host with a name for it). The command prints a link and a code: open the link while signed in here and approve.
steps.guard: Install the egress guard once, as root. Without it the host connects but can't start any sandbox.
steps.run: Start the daemon. To keep it running across logouts and reboots, run it as a systemd user service.

enroll.docsPath: (guide: {{path}} in the WS Sandbox Proxy source repository)

statusHint.stale: No recent heartbeat. The daemon may be down or unreachable, so work sent to it may not start until it is back.
statusHint.quarantined: The daemon is running, but the server refuses its inventory, so the host takes no work. It keeps retrying on its own; there is nothing to start.
statusHint.reconnecting: The daemon connected recently but did not stay connected. It retries on its own. If this lasts, check its log with journalctl --user -u wssp-host.
statusHint.offline: The daemon has not connected recently. Start it with wssp host run, or check its log with journalctl --user -u wssp-host.
statusHint.never: The daemon has not connected yet.
statusHint.revoked: This host's credential was revoked. Enroll it again to reconnect.
statusHint.deleting: The host is removed once its stopped sandboxes, transfers and unfinished work are gone. It accepts no new sandboxes.

quarantineReason.released_instance_present: Quarantine reason: this host still runs a sandbox the server already released. It clears once that sandbox is destroyed.
quarantineReason.unknown_sandbox: Quarantine reason: this host reported a sandbox the server has no record of.
quarantineReason.foreign_sandbox: Quarantine reason: this host reported a sandbox that belongs to another host.
quarantineReason.deleted_instance_present: Quarantine reason: this host still has a sandbox the server already deleted.
quarantineReason.generation_ahead: Quarantine reason: this host reported a sandbox generation the server never sent.
quarantineReason.lease_ahead: Quarantine reason: this host reported a sandbox lease the server never sent.
quarantineReason.lease_regressed: Quarantine reason: this host reported an older lease than the one it acknowledged.
quarantineReason.lease_mismatch: Quarantine reason: this host's lease for a sandbox disagrees with the server's.
quarantineReason.other: Quarantine reason: this host's inventory disagrees with the server's records.

drain.hint: Draining refuses new sandboxes, restarts and templates on this host. Running sandboxes keep running.
drain.drainingHint_one: No new work is admitted. {{count}} live sandbox remains.
drain.drainingHint_other: No new work is admitted. {{count}} live sandboxes remain.
drain.drainedHint: No live sandboxes remain. Retained disks and unfinished work can still block deletion.
drain.offloadHint: Copy this host's stopped sandboxes to the image store and free their disks here once another host they may use could restore them.
drain.offloadingHint: Stopped sandboxes are being offloaded to the image store. A disk stays here while no other eligible host could restore it.

daemon.label: Daemon
daemon.unsupportedHint: This daemon cannot run sandboxes on this machine.

egress.incusHint: This host can't create sandboxes: its daemon reported that it can't enforce outbound network rules. The daemon's log names the reason, for example an Incus release older than 6.14, a missing network ACL extension, or an Incus daemon it couldn't query. Fix that, then restart the daemon.
egress.fakeHint: This host can't create sandboxes: the fake runtime never enforces outbound network rules. Run wssp host run --runtime incus to run sandboxes.
egress.title: Network

guard.label: Network guard

state.offline: Reported while the host is connected
state.incus_server_shared: Another daemon uses this Incus server

reason.unknown: The daemon hasn't reported a network guard on this host.
reason.guard_unreachable: The daemon can't reach the network guard: it isn't installed or isn't running.
reason.guard_not_ok: The network guard reports that it can't enforce its rules.
reason.guard_quarantined: The network guard quarantined this host because a firewall or network setting is outside the supported packet path. Run wssp host guard status on the host to see which one.
reason.guard_lease_expired: The network guard stopped renewing its health report.
reason.guard_outdated: The network guard is older than this daemon and must be upgraded.
reason.guard_root_source: The root blocklist (/etc/wssp/egress-blocklist) is invalid. Fix it with sudoedit.
reason.guard_deployment_source: The network guard couldn't apply this deployment's blocklist.
reason.host_firewall_blocks_sandboxes: This host's firewall (ufw, firewalld or Docker's forwarding policy) drops traffic on the sandbox bridges, so sandboxes would get no address, DNS or internet.
reason.incus_server_shared: Another wssp daemon uses this host's Incus server, and only one daemon per Incus server is supported. Running sandboxes keep running. Stop the other daemon; the host log names it.

guard.install: Install or upgrade the guard by running this on the host as the user that runs the daemon. It needs root, so you run it yourself; wssp host guard status shows the details.
guard.firewall: Run this on the host to add the minimal firewall rules (DHCP, DNS and the login proxy in from the sandbox bridges, plus routing). It prints each rule, and the network guard still enforces every block. Use --configure-firewalld instead on firewalld hosts.

egress.openForOthers: Open internet for other users' sandboxes
egress.off: Off: other users' sandboxes use allowlist mode
egress.openForOthersWarning: Other users' sandboxes on this host can reach the internet from its IP address, and you're responsible for that traffic. The domain blocklist is best-effort.
egress.openUnsupported: This host's daemon can't serve open internet yet, so every sandbox here runs in allowlist mode. Upgrade the daemon.
egress.guestSudoForOthersOff: Off: other users' sandboxes start without root
egress.guestSudoForOthersHint: Other users' sandboxes on this host may run as root inside their VM unless you turn this off. Set it on the host with {{command}}.

edit.title: Edit host
edit.description: Rename this host. Resource budgets and storage are configured locally on its daemon.
edit.label: Name

delete.title: Delete {{name}}?
delete.description: The host and its credentials are removed. If it still has stopped sandboxes or unfinished work, deletion waits for them and the host accepts no new sandboxes meanwhile. This cannot be undone.
delete.typePrompt: Type the host's slug to confirm
delete.blockedLive: Delete is available once no sandboxes are live on this host. Drain it and wait until it is drained.
delete.pending: Deletion is pending until the host's remaining sandboxes and work are gone.

forget.title: Forget {{name}}?
forget.description: Use this only for a host that will never come back. Stopped sandboxes whose disks are in the image store leave the host and restore elsewhere on their next start; their copies on this host are forgotten. A sandbox that may still be running there refuses the forget. Other sandboxes and work still block deletion. This cannot be undone.
forget.done_one: Host forgotten. {{count}} sandbox now restores from the image store.
forget.done_other: Host forgotten. {{count}} sandboxes now restore from the image store.
forget.pending_one: {{count}} sandbox now restores from the image store. Deletion is pending until the host's remaining sandboxes and work are gone.
forget.pending_other: {{count}} sandboxes now restore from the image store. Deletion is pending until the host's remaining sandboxes and work are gone.

vmCapacity.title: Live resource capacity
vmCapacity.stale: Stored report is stale; new placement needs a current report.
vmCapacity.never: No VM capacity report. New starts wait for admission.
vmCapacity.hint: RAM holds include guest RAM plus fixed host overhead. vCPU is summed independently of the per-VM cap. These are commitments, not measured usage. Shrinking a budget preserves existing holds.
vmCapacity.overcommitted: Running sandboxes use more than this host allows
vmCapacity.vcpuBudgetHint: The vCPU budget is schedulable vCPU, not CPU threads. Unless the operator sets --sandbox-vcpu-budget (or sandbox_vcpu_budget in the daemon's TOML), the daemon sets it to {{multiplier}} × the host's CPU threads (at most {{max}}), so sandboxes may overcommit the CPUs up to {{multiplier}}×.

storage.title: Local storage pools
storage.retainedHint: Stopped and uncertain sandboxes retain their root commitments. Only confirmed deletion on the original healthy pool releases them; unavailable storage can block host deletion indefinitely.

source.explicit: Set in the host config file (capacity_gib)

storage.derived: Total-based cap {{total}} GiB · effective {{effective}} GiB · persisted ceiling {{ceiling}} GiB
storage.limited: Free space or the persisted ceiling limits this cap. Only an explicit local capacity_gib override can raise it; review shared backing headroom and reconnect.
storage.hint: This limit counts each sandbox disk at its full size; it does not physically separate them. Leave free space for cached images. Draining stops new sandboxes from using this storage, and a stopped sandbox needs healthy storage to start again.

sharing.ownerLocalCaps: Your own host: RAM and vCPU limits don't apply in your own pool.
sharing.contributionNotice: Contributing allows foreign guests to consume your host budget and send traffic from your network/IP. Withdrawal or lost access stops guests only when no other permitted pool path fits. Foreign disks remain for the accepted pool grace, up to 30 days. Host deletion waits for positive cleanup proof, potentially longer with offline or dead storage.
sharing.trust: Users of a pool with foreign hosts must trust those host operators. An incus-admin host user can reach every VM on that host. API restrictions and disabling dashboard host terminals do not isolate guests from local administrators. The pool owner manages the operator set; current membership does not guarantee future operators.
sharing.forwarding: Accept explicitly after signing in. Bearer acceptance can grant access to a different account than the invited email; forwarding the link can transfer that access. Email-only acceptance requires the verified target email.
sharing.forwardingInviter: The invitation link works like a key: anyone who has it and an account here can accept it with the bearer option, so send it only to the person you invite. The email-only option needs the invited address, verified.
sharing.unsent: Email delivery is unconfirmed. Copy the link now; retrying rotates it.
sharing.emptyShared: No pools are shared with you yet.
